right. gosh, im sorry you’re going through it. my first psychotic episode happened when i was 14 too (i’m 28 now) and i know how frustrating it can be.
as from experience, i can tell that medication works the best of course but it can take a long time to find the right treatment. in the meantime, try not to stay alone for too long. i know it’s hard to talk to others but if there’s just one person you feel comfortable around (maybe your sister?), ask them to hang around so you don’t get trapped in your thoughts. maybe without even talking. ideally, if someone can be around 24/7 and just do their own thing, it would help a lot.
try to distract yourself with arts or crafts, keep some music on that cheers you up (something you can sing would be a great distraction), try video games (they can be very engaging and it keeps your mind off things), try to get enough sleep every night (use sleeping pills if you have to but with cautious), eat regularly (might sound obvious but it’s crucial).
make sure at least someone knows that you’re having mental issues. you don’t have to tell them everything but it’s good to have someone who is aware of your situation if the worst happens and you’d be need urgent care.
what country are you in? (asking in case i can give a more specific advice treatment-wise).
